originalTitle: US stocks: S&P closes at record high as soft jobs report eases rate-hike concerns
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a good day on Friday, with the S&P (a measure of how well the stock market is doing) reaching its highest point ever. This happened because there was a surprise increase in job losses, which made people think that interest rates might not go up as much as expected. This, combined with good earnings reports from companies and lower oil prices, made investors happy and caused the market to go up. The lower oil prices helped calm fears about inflation, which is when prices for things like food and housing rise too quickly. Overall, it was a positive day for the stock market, with many factors coming together to push it to a new high.

originalTitle: Market cuts odds of Fed hike after jobs data, but economists still see case for tightening
simplifiedContent: Here's a simple explanation of the news: Recently, the job market didn't do as well as expected in July, which has made people think that the Federal Reserve (the group in charge of interest rates) might not raise interest rates next month. Because of this, the stock market is now guessing that a rate increase is less likely to happen. Some people at the Federal Reserve still think interest rates should go up to control inflation, but others are not so sure. The Federal Reserve is keeping a close eye on inflation to help make its decision about what to do with interest rates. This matters because changes in interest rates can affect the economy and the stock market.

originalTitle: Dollar falls against yen, euro as weak US jobs data clouds Fed outlook
simplifiedContent: The value of the US dollar went down compared to other major currencies, like the yen and euro, on Friday. This happened because the US job market didn't do as well as expected in July, with some jobs being lost. Even though the number of unemployed people decreased, fewer people were working or looking for jobs than in a long time. This surprising news makes it uncertain what the Federal Reserve (the "Fed") will do with interest rates. The change in the dollar's value and the job market news are connected because they can affect the Fed's decisions, which in turn can impact the overall economy.

originalTitle: Short-Term Treasuries Cap Biggest Weekly Rally Since May on Data
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: the US government's short-term debt (called Treasuries) had a big increase in value this week. This happened because a recent report on jobs in the US was weaker than expected, which made investors think that the Federal Reserve won't raise interest rates as much as they thought. As a result, investors became more interested in buying these short-term Treasuries, which caused their value to go up. This is the biggest weekly increase in value for these short-term Treasuries since May. This matters because it shows how investors are reacting to changes in the economy and what they think the Federal Reserve will do next.

originalTitle: Treasury yields fall as jobs report dashes hike bets
simplifiedContent: The US government recently released a report about jobs, and it had an effect on the stock market. Because of this report, people are now less likely to think that interest rates will go up soon. As a result, the "yields" on US government bonds, also known as Treasuries, have gone down. This means that investors can now earn less money from lending to the government by buying these bonds. The change in yields is important because it can influence the overall direction of the stock market and affect investors' decisions.

originalTitle: Gold hits seven-week high as weak US jobs data dents rate hike bets
simplifiedContent: The price of gold has gone up to its highest point in seven weeks. This happened because there was some disappointing news about jobs in the US, which made people think that interest rates might not go up as quickly as they thought. As a result, people are investing more in gold, which is why its price is rising. This matters because it shows how the job market can affect the economy and investors' decisions. The increase in gold's price is a reaction to the unexpected news about the US job market.
